newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rail traffic at highest level in 1996.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rail traffic at highest level in 1996.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic hit its highest level so far this year, but a big drop in grain car loadings stalled further gains, a railroad group said Thursday.
The Association of American Railroads said carload originations peaked at 359,752 in the week ended August 31. But compared to a year earlier, they were down 1.3 percent from 364,355.
"Substantial declines in grain and grain mill products dampened what otherwise would have been an even more robust week," AAR chief economist Harvey Levine said.
Grain carloadings slumped to 22,521 in the week, a 24.4 percent decline from 29,795 last year. Grain mill product loadings were at 9,629, down 6.5 percent from 10,294 a year ago.
Overall trailer and container traffic in the week was up 3.3 percent from a year ago 169,089 cars, versus 163,669 last year.
The group reported ton miles in the week of 26.7 billion, down 0.7 percent from 26.9 billion a year ago. A ton-mile equals one ton of freight hauled one mile.

Carloadings of lumber and wood products totalled 6,318 in the week, up 10.1 percent from 5,741 a year ago. Carloadings of motor vehicles and parts were at 20,679, up 8.4 percent from 19,068 last year.
Loadings of chemicals were at 33,319 cars in the week, up 2.8 percent from 32,412 last year. There were 138,762 carloads of coal in the week, up 1.8 percent from 136,327 a year ago.
